statistical_criterion: Agent's numeric/text answer must fall within a 95% prediction interval derived from three independent manual reproductions of the capsule; accounts for stochastic outputs (17/181 questions are stochastic) (p. 7)
Difference ≤10% of original = small; >10% = large; used to derive the 0/25/50/75/100 score, collapsed to full-vs-not for this operationalization
Same ≤10%/>10% threshold, mapped to 5-level score per Table 2

"Exact" = results "agreed exactly with the paper, up to the decimals printed in the paper or shown in the figures"; "Qualitative" = "small differences... but still agreed with the abstract-level findings"; "Not at all" = "results that were in conflict with the abstract-level findings" (Appendix B, Preregistered analysis plan: Replication outcomes).
margin of error, and congruence of statistical measures (coefficient signs/CIs/hypothesis decisions (p. 4)

"Fully reproducible" = all numbers/figures match up to minor rounding; "partially reproducible" = differences beyond rounding for some tables, but results qualitatively similar or main results hold while secondary/robustness results differ (p.973–974)

"Functional equivalence": outcomes derived from independent code execution must be consistent ("the outcomes derived from their deterministic code execution... are consistent, even if CA and CI differ textually", p.10173), operationalized via automated GPT-4o comparison scored 0/1 (Appendix Table 22: "If the output of the two code snippets provide the same values for the same statistics and lead to the same conclusion to the question, please score 1. Otherwise, score 0.")
X/N — statistically significant effect in same direction as original, at 5% level, two-sided p-value
